entities.label: Movement
entities.summary: A German art school and movement (1919-1933) that unified fine arts, crafts, and technology under the principle that form follows function. Founded by Walter Gropius in Weimar, the Bauhaus trained a generation of designers, architects, and artists whose minimalist aesthetic — clean lines, functional design, industrial materials — defined 20th-century modernism.
